extraction.name: Visual Question Answering Datasets
extraction.description: A review of Visual Question Answering (VQA) datasets including DAQUAR, COCO-QA, The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA and SYNTH-VQA), FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, and SHAPES. These datasets enable VQA systems to be trained and evaluated for answering text-based questions about images.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafle and Christopher Kanan
extraction.publisher: Chester F. Carlson Center for Imaging Science, Rochester Institute of Technology
extraction.citeAs: Kafle, K., & Kanan, C. (2017). Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv preprint arXiv:1610.01465v4.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Multiple VQA datasets were created using different collection processes. DAQUAR used images from NYU-DepthV2 Dataset with manually generated questions. COCO-QA derived QA pairs from COCO image captions using an NLP algorithm. The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA) employed Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' with separate workers generating answers. SYNTH-VQA used synthetic cartoon images with 50,000 scenes. FM-IQA collected questions and answers in Chinese with English translations. Visual Genome used two modes: free-form questions and region-specific questions prompted by bounding boxes. Visual7W is a subset of Visual Genome.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Surveys
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from: NYU-DepthV2 Dataset (DAQUAR), Microsoft Common Objects in Context (COCO) dataset containing 328,000 images with 91 common object categories and over 2 million labeled instances (COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome), YFCC100M/Flickr100M (Visual Genome, Visual7W), and synthetic cartoon images (SYNTH-VQA).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For COCO-QA, longer sentences were broken into smaller chunks for processing by the NLP algorithm. For FDA model evaluation, object labels and bounding boxes were obtained from COCO annotations during training, and during testing, labels were obtained by classifying each bounding box using ResNet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: COCO-VQA: Three questions per image were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers who were asked to 'Stump a smart robot.' A separate pool of workers generated ten answers per question. SYNTH-VQA: 3 questions per scene with 10 ground truth answers per question. DAQUAR-consensus: An average of five human annotated ground truth answers per question were collected. Visual Genome: Used free-form method where annotators asked any question, and region-specific method where workers were prompted to ask questions about specific image regions using descriptive bounding-box annotations. Visual7W: Contains 'telling' questions (text-based answers) and 'pointing' questions (selecting correct bounding box). For multiple-choice, plausible answers were collected by prompting annotators to answer questions without seeing the image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For The VQA Dataset, inter-human agreement is about 83.3%. Inter-human agreement is especially poor for 'Why' questions, with over 59% having less than three annotators giving exactly the same answer. More than 13% of yes/no answers have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. The evaluation metric AccuracyVQA awards full score if the algorithm agrees with three or more annotators out of ten.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: SYNTH-VQA human cartoon models span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential applications include aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images both on the web and in the real world. VQA could improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content and be used for image retrieval without using image meta-data or tags.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: COCO-VQA contains many subjective, opinion-seeking questions that do not have a single objective answer. Yes/no answers span about 38% of all questions, with almost 59% answered with 'yes.' Language biases allow relatively simple image-blind algorithms to achieve 49.6% accuracy using the question alone. Questions tend to have strong bias, with the question severely constraining the kinds of answers expected. The way questions are phrased strongly biases the answer. COCO-QA questions are limited to four types (object, color, counting, location). Visual Genome and Visual7W exclude binary questions altogether. Natural image datasets tend to have more consistent context and biases (e.g., street scenes more likely to have dogs than zebras). SHAPES dataset is completely balanced and free of bias with 244 unique questions asked about each of 64 images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small to successfully train and evaluate complex models, contains exclusively indoor scenes constraining question variety, and images have significant clutter and extreme lighting conditions. Human accuracy is only 50.2%. COCO-QA has awkwardly phrased questions with grammatical errors due to flaws in the NLP algorithm, and is limited to four question types. The VQA Dataset contains subjective questions, opinion-seeking questions, and questions seeking explanations or verbose descriptions. Many questions can be accurately answered without using the image due to language biases. FM-IQA requires human judges for evaluation, making it impractical. Visual Genome's long-tailed answer distribution (1000 most frequent answers cover only 65% vs 82% for COCO-VQA) makes open-ended evaluation challenging. Diversity in answers may artificially stem from variations in phrasing. Dataset bias significantly impairs ability to evaluate VQA algorithms, with harder questions like 'Why' being comparatively rare.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. VQA can be considered a component of a Turing Test for image understanding. The datasets are used to train and evaluate VQA systems capable of answering text-based questions about images, encompassing sub-problems including object recognition, object detection, attribute classification, scene classification, counting, spatial relationships, and common sense reasoning.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: COCO-VQA: 3 questions per image, 10 answers per question. SYNTH-VQA: 3 questions per scene, 10 ground truth answers per question. DAQUAR-consensus: Average of 5 human annotated ground truth answers per question. Visual Genome: Average of 17 QA pairs per image.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: For COCO-QA, an NLP algorithm was used to derive QA pairs from COCO image captions. Natural language parsers were used in Neural Module Network (NMN) framework to find sub-tasks in questions and infer required layout.
